gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a UST laser TV like the Hisense L9Q lists no 12V trigger output, so a floor-rising screen can only follow the projector's power through a dongle on the projector's USB port. Elite says its dongle 'uses the projector's USB 5V Type A power supply to send a radio frequency signal', so the screen reacts to that port's voltage rather than to the picture.
standout_why: Compared against projector-screen-guide.com (rank 1), primeareviews.com, projectorverdict.com/best-motorized-projector-screen and allinprojectors.com. projector-screen-guide.com already explains the main reason a plan fails: UST ALR/CLR material only works with light coming steeply from below, and VIVIDSTORM and Elite say their UST screens don't work with ceiling-mounted or standard-throw projectors. It also covers the Kestrel's 12V trigger. projectorverdict.com says 'Not every projector has a 12V trigger output, so check yours first' and that VIVIDSTORM's dongle 'does not work with every projector'. allinprojectors.com mentions USB auto-sync on AWOL and NothingProjector. None of them says that UST laser TVs list no 12V trigger, that a USB trigger works by sensing the port's 5 V, or that Elite's USB trigger only works with SWIFT-RC1 screens. So the rivals have part of this but not the reason.
decides: This settles whether the screen rises and lowers by itself with the projector, not whether the picture works. The material question (UST screen for a UST projector) is already answered by the rivals. With a 12V-less UST laser TV such as the L9Q, auto-sync depends on the USB dongle. VIVIDSTORM S PRO/S PRO P include a dongle but flag it as 'not compatible with all projectors'. The Elite Kestrel CLR5/TT2 CLR3 need the optional ZUSBV-RC1. The page should tell the shopper to check that the projector has a USB Type-A port that turns off when the projector turns off. If it doesn't, use the screen's RF remote or app instead. This doesn't change the pick, but it should be a caveat on every UST floor-riser.

findings.product: Elite Screens Wireless USB Trigger ZUSBV-RC1
findings.label: How the USB trigger senses the projector
findings.value: Elite says it 'Uses the projector's USB 5V Type A power supply to send a radio frequency signal'. It is 'designed for projectors with a USB Type-A power port (5V)'. RF range is 49 ft (15 m).
findings.source_title: Electric Screen Accessory – Wireless USB Trigger ZUSBV-RC1 (Elite Screens)
findings.note: Maker product page. The dongle reacts to the port's 5 V, so it fires when the port powers on and off, not when the picture does. The page gives no price.

findings.product: Elite Screens Wireless USB Trigger ZUSBV-RC1
findings.label: Which screens it works with
findings.value: Elite lists it as 'Compatible with all electric drop-down / floor-rising motorized screens with SWIFT-RC1 control system', naming the Kestrel Tab-Tension CLR 5, Kestrel Tab-Tension 3 CineGrey 4D and Kestrel Tab-Tension 2 CLR 3. It does not work with non-RC1 screens.
findings.source_title: Electric Screen Accessory – Wireless USB Trigger ZUSBV-RC1 (Elite Screens)

findings.label: The trigger input reads voltage, not a data signal
findings.value: Elite's FAQ, for projectors with no 12V port: 'You will need to splice your USB cable with an RJ45 cable. A USB has 4 wires, but you will only need the red and black.' It notes this is not compatible with the SWIFT-RC1 control system, which uses RJ50.
findings.source_title: Elite Screens FAQ: My projector does not have a 12V trigger port but it does have a USB port…
findings.note: In USB the red and black wires are +5 V and ground. Wiring only those two into the 5-12 V trigger input shows the screen moves on voltage alone.

findings.label: Ports listed: no trigger output
findings.value: USB: '1 x USB 3.0, 1 x USB 2.0, 1 x USB 3.0 type C'. Other ports: 2× HDMI 2.1, 2× HDMI 2.0, LAN, RF antenna, earphone out, 1 optical. No 12V trigger is listed.
